newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa discussing fx control moves with banks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa discussing fx control moves with banks.

text.p: South Africa's Reserve Bank would be discussing details of the relaxation of exchange controls, announced in Wednesday's budget, with commercial banks over the next two to three weeks, governor Chris Stals said on Friday.

Following these discussions the central bank would be in a better position to advise government as to how much individuals should be allowed to invest overseas or hold in local foreign currency bank accounts, he told parliament's finance committee.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said in his budget that individuals would be allowed to invest an unspecified amount offshore from July 1.

Issues to be resolved included how banks should cover individuals' foreign currency acounts with foreign assets, whether this should form part of the bank's balance sheet for capital adequacy purposes, whether a bank would have to hold cash reserves at the Reserve Bank against these liabilities and how it would affect liquid asset requirements.

"Those are things we will have to sort out with the banks, and we will do so in the next two or three weeks...Once we have gone through that whole exercise it will be easier to advise the minister on the amount that should be fixed for each individual to invest outside of the country or through the banks," Stals said.
